Thought: I need to determine the acidity of the given compounds and arrange them from most acidic to least acidic. Let me analyze each compound in SMILES notation.

1. CC(C)=O: This is acetone (propanone), a ketone. Ketones are generally not acidic.

2. CC(N)=O: This is acetamide. Amides are weakly acidic.

3. CC1=CC=C(S(=O)(O)=O)C=C1: This is p-toluenesulfonic acid. Sulfonic acids are strong acids.

To determine acidity, I need to consider the stability of the conjugate base after deprotonation. The more stable the conjugate base, the more acidic the compound.

Sulfonic acids (CC1=CC=C(S(=O)(O)=O)C=C1) are much stronger acids than ketones or amides because the negative charge in the conjugate base is stabilized by resonance and the electronegative oxygen atoms.

Amides (CC(N)=O) are generally more acidic than ketones (CC(C)=O) due to the electron-withdrawing effect of the nitrogen atom.

So the correct ordering from most acidic to least acidic would be:
CC1=CC=C(S(=O)(O)=O)C=C1 (sulfonic acid) > CC(N)=O (amide) > CC(C)=O (ketone)

Looking at the options, this matches option D.
